newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ukraine's Kuchma wants re-election to help reforms.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma wants re-election to help reforms.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, in an article published in a French newspaper on Monday, said he would seek re-election in 1999 to push through free market reforms and seek closer ties with the European Union.
Kuchma, writing in Le Monde, said he expected a modest economic upturn in 1997. But he added that Ukraine would need a stiff new round of reforms to stimulate longer-term growth.
"I hereby announce my intention to stand in the presidential election, currently fixed for the month of October 1999," he said.

"The main domestic challenge today is the return of economic growth," Kuchma, elected two years ago, added. He forecast economic growth of 1.7 percent for 1997 after years of shrinking following the former Soviet republic's shift from communism.
Kuchma appealed to foreign nations to help Ukraine with the reforms, including simplifying the tax system, bolstering private enterprise and overhauling agriculture.
"All that requires foreign investment. Ukraine has so far received just over a billion dollars from abroad for all private investments, when it needs several billion every year," he wrote.

He said Ukraine had cooperated especially with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) over its economic reforms but that it "seriously needed" other financing. Foreign donors would meet in Paris on October 24 and 25 to assess 1997 needs.

Kuchma reaffirmed his plan, announced earlier this year, for Ukraine to join the 15-nation EU in the next century. Ukraine's reform plans "will contribute....to the economic prosperity and political stability of Europe," he said.
He said inflation had fallen under his leadership to 25 percent last year from just over 10 percent in 1993 while the budget deficit had contracted to 2.4 percent of gross domestic product.
The Ukrainian currency had stabilised and exports had risen by about 20 percent in the first six months of 1996, he added.
